content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

System: Source Code owned by Engineer role.

Most notes say Traci is an Analyst, full_time. One note (Security DB) says contractor with basic security training.

Discrepancy: Most databases say full_time Analyst, Security says contractor basic training.

Since most agents confirm full_time Analyst, and the Security note is the outlier. But the Security DB might be the authoritative one for employment type? Actually the HR agent would be the one for employment type. Which agent wrote note 6? "Security DB shows..." - the Security agent.

Note 1 seems to be from HR (role looked up in own database), employment type looked up. Notes 2-5 from IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities confirmed. Note 6 is Security which contradicts.

Hmm. How to resolve? The majority consensus says full_time Analyst. Per policy, full_time employees can get up to write for systems they don't own (Source Code owned by Engineer, not Analyst). So max is write.

Requested admin > max write, so grant write.

Even under contractor interpretation, contractor with basic training maxes at read, grant read. But majority says full_time.

Given most agents agree, and the policy for full_time Analyst gives max write. Requested admin exceeds write, so grant write.

Let me submit decision: write.

Reason: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst per HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write for systems they don't own. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant write. (One conflicting note from Security claims contractor, but multiple corroborating records support full-time.)
